Passed 2025-06-25. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Directs the Maine Arts Commission to study federal and national efforts to protect artists from copyright infringement by businesses and others promoting, creating, disseminating or using artificial intelligence software applications, and to study federal and national efforts to monitor educational use of copyrighted work. The commission must report findings and any suggested legislation to the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs by December 3, 2025. The resolve provides one time funding of $25,000 for a consultant and allows the commission to accept outside funding.

Who it applies to

  • Maine Arts Commission
  • Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • not stated in the text

Obligations

  • Study federal and national efforts to protect artists from copyright infringement by businesses and others promoting, creating, disseminating or using artificial intelligence software applications and federal and national efforts to monitor the educational use of copyrighted work (Sec. 1)
  • Consult with the Office of the Attorney General on the subject of the study (Sec. 1)
  • Report its findings, including any suggested legislation, to the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs by December 3, 2025 (Sec. 1)

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • No direct obligations or prohibitions are imposed on organisations deploying artificial intelligence; the resolve only directs a study and report (Sec. 1)
  • The Maine Arts Commission may suggest legislation to the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, which may report out a bill to the Second Regular Session of the 132nd Legislature, potentially leading to future regulation of AI deployment (Sec. 1)
  • One time funds of $25,000 are provided for a consultant to research and analyze the impact of unauthorized usage by artificial intelligence on an artist's work (Sec. 3)

Notable exemptions

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • Conduct the study described in Sec. 1 (Sec. 1)
  • Consult with the Office of the Attorney General (Sec. 1)
  • Consider relevant work of the Maine State Cultural Affairs Council, National Endowment for the Humanities, National Endowment for the Arts, American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers, proposed federal No Fakes Act of 2024, proposed federal No AI FRAUD Act, Tennessee's Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security Act of 2024, and case law including Waits v. Frito-Lay, Inc. and Midler v. Ford Motor Co. (Sec. 1)
  • Report findings and any suggested legislation to the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs by December 3, 2025 (Sec. 1)
  • May accept grants, private contributions and any additional outside funding for the study (Sec. 2)
  • Use the $25,000 one time General Fund allocation for a consultant to research and analyze the impact of unauthorized usage by artificial intelligence on an artist's work (Sec. 3)

 Resolve, Directing the Maine Arts Commission to Study Federal and
National Efforts to Protect Artists from Copyright Infringement by Artificial
 Intelligence Companies and Users and to Monitor Educational Use

 Sec. 1. Maine Arts Commission study. Resolved: That the Maine Arts
Commission shall study federal and national efforts to protect artists from copyright
infringement by businesses and others promoting, creating, disseminating or using artificial
intelligence software applications and federal and national efforts to monitor the
educational use of copyrighted work. The commission shall consult with the Office of the
Attorney General on the subject of the study. In its study, the commission may consider
any relevant work of or obtain information from the Maine State Cultural Affairs Council,
the National Endowment for the Humanities, the National Endowment for the Arts and the
American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers, as well as any other similar
organizations. The commission may also consider the proposed federal No Fakes Act of
2024, the proposed federal No AI FRAUD Act and Tennessee's Ensuring Likeness, Voice,
and Image Security Act of 2024, as well as other relevant law or case law, including Waits
v. Frito-Lay, Inc., 978 F.2d 1093 (9th Cir. 1992) and Midler v. Ford Motor Co., 849 F.2d
460 (9th Cir. 1988). The commission shall report its findings, including any suggested
legislation, to the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs by
December 3, 2025. The joint standing committee may report out a bill to the Second
Regular Session of the 132nd Legislature based on the report.
 Sec. 2. Funding. Resolved: That the Maine Arts Commission may accept grants,
private contributions and any additional outside funding for the study under this resolve.
 Sec. 3. Appropriations and allocations. Resolved: That the following
appropriations and allocations are made.
ARTS COMMISSION, MAINE
